submission.natural_language_explanation: N2683+ is a retrospective, token-keyed lexical detector: it fires on content words of written informational/attributional English - the vocabulary of producing, recording, sourcing and analysing text and data (according, ask/asked, write/wrote/written, read, said, author, question, word, text, sentence, record, figure, data, analysis, method, study, document, article, publish, editor, label, survey, interview, program) and the expository connectives (also, additionally, during, within, among, moreover, furthermore, based) - and on the non-initial BPE pieces of long Graeco-Latin words (versely in in|versely, stract in ab|stract, ivariate in bi|variate, izontal in hor|izontal, ologies, ologically, ophysical, opathy, otype, atively, ively, uments). It stays near its floor on function words and on narrative, emotional and generic abstract vocabulary (happiness, love, fear, dream, desire, prosperity, death, truth, freedom, time, people, world, life, work, way, thing, cat): context moves a given trigger token by at most about a third of the scale and never turns a lexical non-member into a peak.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
The marsh at the north end of the bay had been drained twice in the last century and twice allowed to flood again, so that by the time anyone thought to protect it the ground belonged to no one in particular. Reeds took it first, then the birds that hide in reeds, then a slow argument between the county and the farmers about who should pay to keep the ditches clear.

The argument ran for six years. Each side hired people to measure the thing it cared about. The county counted birds, the farmers counted lost grazing, and the numbers never touched, because a bird is not a pound of mutton and nobody could agree on how to weigh one against the other.

Then the water came back on its own, as water does, after a winter of storms pushed the sea over the wall and left a shallow lagoon where the drainage channel had been. For a season the place looked ruined: brown water, drowned grass, a smell that carried for half a mile.

By the following summer the lagoon was full of fish, and the fish brought the birds, and the birds brought people with binoculars and thermos flasks and walking boots. A raised walkway went in, paid for partly by the county and partly by a fund the farmers had set up. The irony was lost on nobody. The same men who had fought the scheme for six years now leaned on the rail at weekends and pointed out herons to strangers.

There was a small wooden hide at the southern end, and a notice board with a map of the reserve and a line about keeping dogs on a lead. Someone had scratched a rude phrase into the paint, and someone else had painted over it, and the paint did not match, so the phrase was still faintly there under the new layer for anyone who looked.

When the work was finished, the author of the county's final report had written a short preface describing the marsh as a lesson in patience. The record shows that the first proposal was tabled in 1987, and that the budget attached to it came to less than the cost of a single storm.

At dusk the tide pulled back from the harbour wall and left a skin of wet sand shining under the lamps. Old Tomas walked the length of it with a bucket, picking up whatever the water had given back: a cracked blue plate, a length of rope, one leather boot with no laces. He had done this every evening since the boats stopped coming, and he did it without hurry, stopping now and then to look at the hills where the light was going out.

His granddaughter Mira watched from the kitchen window. She was fifteen and restless, and the village felt to her like a held breath. Nothing happened here. The same faces, the same weather, the same three buses a week climbing the coast road and turning back before dark. She had begun to keep a private list of places she would go, cities stacked on cities, each one louder and brighter than the last.

Tomas came in with the bucket and set it by the stove. He washed the plate under the tap, dried it on his sleeve, and put it on the shelf with the others. There were eleven plates there now, none of them matching, and he liked them better than the good china his wife had kept behind glass.

'You could sell those,' Mira offered from the doorway. 'Someone would pay.' She was not being cruel. She simply could not see why a man would carry broken things home.

He thought about it while the kettle heated. 'Maybe,' he answered at last. 'But then I would have to go and find more.' He grinned at his own joke, and she rolled her eyes and went back to the window.

She folded the map into a small square and hid it under the mattress and lay awake thinking about the sound of four hundred miles of road.
